source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §E Subordination and chapter-wide exam synthesis

coverage.scope: E. §510(c) equitable subordination, Mobile Steel, Taylor/Deep Rock, Pepper, Clark Pipe, Noland and CF&I; integrated exam decision trees and calculations
coverage.note: These §E decisions are discussed in textbook prose, NOT full excerpted opinions.

topics.title: E. §510(c) Equitable Subordination: Case-Specific Misconduct and Fairness
topics.description: Historic Deep Rock/Pepper, Mobile Steel three-part framework, insider vs outsider and Noland/CF&I limits.

entries.title: §510(c)(1): court can subordinate otherwise allowed claim
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §E Subordination and chapter-wide exam synthesis
entries.summary: Court may reorder all or part of claimant's otherwise allowed claim BELOW other allowed claims to remedy inequity; extraordinary narrow remedy.
entries.laymanExplanation: Creditor may really be owed money but gets sent to back of payment line for abusive conduct.
entries.legalExplanation: Different from claim disallowance under §502 and statutory penalty tier §726(a)(4).
entries.examApplication: Check claim is legally valid, then misconduct/priority separately.
entries.examTrap: Don't label subordinated debt automatically fraudulent or invalid.

entries.title: Historical Deep Rock and Pepper v Litton
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §E Subordination and chapter-wide exam synthesis
entries.summary: Taylor v Standard Gas (Deep Rock) subordinated parent that undercapitalized/mismanaged subsidiary; Pepper v Litton subordinated controlling shareholder exploiting corporation for own benefit.
entries.laymanExplanation: Insider who rigs business to put its own loan ahead of others may lose distribution position.
entries.legalExplanation: Foundations codified in 1978 §510(c) with common law development still relevant.
entries.examApplication: On facts of parent-affiliate insider loans, identify domination, capitalization and fairness.
entries.examTrap: A parent stockholder's status alone doesn't require subordination.

entries.title: Mobile Steel: three elements
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §E Subordination and chapter-wide exam synthesis
entries.summary: Common framework: (1) inequitable conduct by claimant; (2) injury to debtor creditors or unfair advantage to claimant; (3) subordination not inconsistent with Code statutory requirements.
entries.laymanExplanation: Bad conduct + harm/unfair gain + consistency with law.
entries.legalExplanation: Courts continue to follow Mobile Steel though Supreme Court later refused broad categorical uses of equitable subordination.
entries.examApplication: Build explicit three-prong heading in essay.
entries.examTrap: Equitable subordination is not just 'judge thinks debt unfair'.

entries.title: Three recurring misconduct categories
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §E Subordination and chapter-wide exam synthesis
entries.summary: (1) fraud/illegality/breach of fiduciary duty; (2) undercapitalization; (3) using debtor as mere instrumentality/alter ego.
entries.laymanExplanation: Lying, intentionally starving subsidiary of cash, or controlling company as personal puppet.
entries.legalExplanation: Evidence must relate to injury or advantage, not only unsavory behavior.
entries.examApplication: In parent company financing hypothetical compare capitalization/records/control and disproportionate benefits.
entries.examTrap: Undercapitalization alone can be fact-intensive; no automatic remedy based solely on hardship.

entries.title: Insider claims get heightened scrutiny
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §E Subordination and chapter-wide exam synthesis
entries.summary: Officer/director/controlling shareholder's dealings closely scrutinized because fiduciary duty and conflict; on material evidence unfair insider conduct, insider may have burden to establish good faith/fairness.
entries.laymanExplanation: When CEO lends to own failing company and gets paid before workers, court closely examines deal.
entries.legalExplanation: Insider status alone isn't violation, but unequal control and duties distinguish ordinary arm's-length creditor.
entries.examApplication: Identify insider §101(31) status, relevant control and insider's explanation of transaction.
entries.examTrap: Don't conclude all insider loans subordinate automatically.

entries.title: Noninsider creditor usually may enforce arm's-length contract
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §E Subordination and chapter-wide exam synthesis
entries.summary: Ordinary independent lender need not save debtor or other creditors; aggressive collection generally not inequitable absent domination, fraud or other serious conduct.
entries.laymanExplanation: Bank can protect its own debt using agreed loan terms, even if debtor gets worse off.
entries.legalExplanation: Clark Pipe originally subordinated lender but on rehearing rejected due to absence of total control beyond arms-length borrowing.
entries.examApplication: Use degree of control: did creditor actually manage debtor as instrumentality?
entries.examTrap: Merely lending less or accelerating collection isn't enough.

entries.title: Noland and CF&I (1996): no categorical subordination by claim type
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §E Subordination and chapter-wide exam synthesis
entries.summary: Supreme Court invalidated broad rule subordinating all government noncompensatory tax penalties without case-specific inequity merely because such claims look punitive; Court did NOT decide whether misconduct is necessary in every case.
entries.laymanExplanation: Court can't invent a new universal payment rule to replace Congress's tax priority.
entries.legalExplanation: Equitable subordination must rest on individual case's equities and avoid conflict with §507 statutory ranking.
entries.examApplication: When fine appears punitive ask whether actual conduct/equities warrant §510(c), and apply §726(a)(4) if applicable.
entries.examTrap: Don't cite these as deciding inequitable conduct always mandatory for all imaginable cases.

entries.title: Subordination extent should address harm, not punish freely
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §E Subordination and chapter-wide exam synthesis
entries.summary: §510(c) grants flexibility to subordinate all or part of claim, but based on unfair creditor advantage or injury; remedy can't override Congress's general ranking for an entire categorical type.
entries.laymanExplanation: If abusive insider gained $30k, court examines tailored remedy rather than automatically erasing $1m valid debt.
entries.legalExplanation: Mobile Steel framework aims to redress injury/advantage; exact measure depends case and applicable law.
entries.examApplication: In exam identify nexus between misconduct and creditors' loss.
entries.examTrap: Don't confuse full claim disallowance and calibrated distribution rank.

entries.title: Claim-type penalty under §726 vs equitable remedy under §510
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §E Subordination and chapter-wide exam synthesis
entries.summary: Noncompensatory penalty often already occupies fourth §726 tier; §510 adds discretionary case-specific remedy where equity proven, not a substitute legislative priority system.
entries.laymanExplanation: Code itself lowers general penalties; court shouldn't reflexively lower already statutorily favored tax penalties too.
entries.examApplication: For claims involving taxes/penalties ask first whether §507 priority applies, then §510 case-specific.
entries.examTrap: §510 isn't free general authority to rewrite distribution structure.

topics.title: Chapter 5 — Exam Map: Claim → Allowance → Priority → Payout → Subordination
topics.description: Comprehensive five-stage issue spotting, case selection and math discipline.

entries.title: Stage 1: classify right as claim and when arose
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §E Subordination and chapter-wide exam synthesis
entries.summary: §101(5)(A) payment or §101(5)(B) equitable payment alternative; prepetition vs later origin via Grossman's exposure and other timing tests; separate notice/due process discharge.
entries.laymanExplanation: Start by asking if creditor has a seat at bankruptcy table at all.
entries.legalExplanation: Referenced cases Kovacs/Apex/Shearin distinguish monetary vs surviving equitable obligation.
entries.examApplication: Use facts of time, legal right and remedy.
entries.examTrap: Never start distribution calculation before classifying obligation.

entries.title: Stage 2: determine allowance and exact petition-date amount
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §E Subordination and chapter-wide exam synthesis
entries.summary: §501 proof/deemed filing, timely/late, §502(b) statutory defenses, valuation/estimation, exclude unmatured interest, landlord and employee damage caps.
entries.laymanExplanation: Valid debt can be chopped down by bankruptcy-specific cap.
entries.legalExplanation: Use Code §502 and any source-era relevant Rules; note no-asset exceptions.
entries.examApplication: Write allowed dollar amount and subsection.
entries.examTrap: Don't assume creditor's face invoice equals allowed claim.

entries.title: Stage 3: secured status, §507 statutory rank and §503 administration
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §E Subordination and chapter-wide exam synthesis
entries.summary: Check valid secured collateral first; priority category §507(a) rank1–10; §503(b) postpetition induced estate transaction/benefit or Reading/§959(b) exception; §507/§364 superpriority; leave ordinary unsecured in §726 tier2.
entries.laymanExplanation: Before splitting pie, take out secured property and put each remaining bill in correct queue.
entries.legalExplanation: Jartran denied priority for locked prepetition ads; N.P. Mining allowed only new operating-law penalties.
entries.examApplication: Mark when labor/goods performed, active operation, state regulation, and caps.
entries.examTrap: A 'high-priority' claim needs specific statutory authority.

entries.title: Stage 4: distributions or reorganization plan confirmation
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §E Subordination and chapter-wide exam synthesis
entries.summary: For Chapter 7 order §726 tiers and calculate pro rata; for Chapters 11/12/13 apply best interests, priority full treatment, disposable income and Chapter11 class voting/cramdown rules as appropriate.
entries.laymanExplanation: Chapter 7 pool is split now; reorganization pays over time under court-approved plan.
entries.legalExplanation: Distinguish liquidation floor and projected future income tests, which can both bind debtor.
entries.examApplication: Use actual estate net equity and class acceptance facts.
entries.examTrap: Don't apply Chapter 11 class voting rules to Chapter 13.

entries.title: Stage 5: challenge inequitable insider/noninsider claims via §510(c)
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §E Subordination and chapter-wide exam synthesis
entries.summary: When claim valid but creditor behaved inequitably, test Mobile Steel and insider control, injury or unfair gain and statutory consistency; §510 changes rank, not original existence.
entries.laymanExplanation: Debt might be real, but creditor may lose favored place in line if abused debtor.
entries.legalExplanation: Noland/CF&I block blanket category-based rewriting of §507 priorities.
entries.examApplication: Analyze impropriety only after allowance/priority in chronology.
entries.examTrap: Do not use equitable subordination as substitute for proof deadline or §502 disallowance.

entries.title: Universal cap formula cheat sheet (book)
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §E Subordination and chapter-wide exam synthesis
entries.summary: Landlord future cap months=max(12,min(0.15×remaining lease months,36)), plus eligible pretermination rent; §502(b)(7) 1 year termination compensation + unpaid due; same-rank payout = fund×claim÷total; §503(b)(9) received prefiling 20 days; reclamation §546(c) received within 45 days and written demand postfiling 20 days.
entries.laymanExplanation: Four numbers to memorize: 12/15%/36, 1 year, 20/45/20 days, proportional payment.
entries.legalExplanation: Caps give ceilings; actual legally enforceable damage and senior ranks may produce much less.
entries.examApplication: Practice 5.2(e) 91-year lease limit 36mo; 5.2(f) $25m/year; 5.3 ratios; leave source problem answers unanswered.
entries.examTrap: Formula entry is study aid, not a response resolving all textbook problems.

entries.title: Regulatory obligations comparison (cross-chapter)
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §E Subordination and chapter-wide exam synthesis
entries.summary: Penn Terra (Chapter4) regulatory nonmoney injunction can proceed under §362(b)(4); Kovacs (Chapter5) receiver turned clean-up into payment claim; Apex Oil mandatory cleanup nonclaim; Midlantic unsafe property abandonment restricted; N.P. Mining new punitive fines during active operation potentially admin.
entries.laymanExplanation: Same pollution facts can present five distinct statutory questions, not one environmental bankruptcy answer.
entries.legalExplanation: Stay exception, discharge claim definition, property abandonment and priority are independent lenses.
entries.examApplication: Read exact issue in fact pattern before selecting case.
entries.examTrap: Do not use a valid §362(b)(4) exception as automatic proof a debt is non-dischargeable.
